title: Browser automation vs raw HTTP — the cost of a real click
hypothesis: Firing the raw request (HTTP-direct / hybrid) is materially faster than driving a real browser click.
method: Approach A (Playwright MutationObserver click), B (raw HTTP-direct, Rust), and C (hybrid: real browser, injected fetch) race the same mock; release→hit on one clock.
conclusion: Raw HTTP is ~4-5x faster than a rendered click, and the hybrid beats the observer by skipping the render->observe->click chain. Browser tails are also much fatter (p95).
decision: Default to C for a real drop (browser cover + near-raw speed); drop to B only with a known endpoint and no CAPTCHA.
